manifest.name: dsh-tool-config-studio
manifest.description: DSH bundle + client plugin: browse every registered tool, edit its configuration, and restore defaults with confidence.
manifest.author: yqd-coder

bundle.text:
# dsh-tool-config-studio bundle patch.
#
# A single web row that mounts the Tool Config Studio panel into the shell.
# The row's name is this package itself: the node half is the package root
# (a no-op `apply`), and the browser half is the built `./client` module
# bundle, which registers the sidebar entry and the main panel keyed
# `tool-config-studio`.
- insert:
    - id: tool-config-studio
      name: 'dsh-tool-config-studio'

readme.text: A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) bundle that turns the tool catalog **and the system settings document** into settings surfaces: **browse every registered tool or system plugin, expand any of them to edit its configuration, and — when you've made a mistake — restore the defaults with a single click.** Installs as a proper DSH plugin from the Plugins page and adds two panels to the sidebar: *Tool Config Studio* (tool defaults) and *System Plugin Studio* (model adapters, default model, and every other plugin that exposes live-editable parameters).

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ⚙ Tool Config Studio                     [  search tools…  ]  [Restore all defaults] │
│  Edit stored defaults for every registered DSH tool.                 │
│                                                                      │

Every DSH tool takes parameters, and a meaningful share of them have tunable, *stored* behavior: how far `read` goes by default, whether `pwsh` jobs run in the background, which scope `list_agents` starts from, how `job_output` waits, the minimum interval a schedule may tick, and so on. Before, the only way to discover or change those defaults was to dig through source or profile patches. Tool Config Studio gives each tool a proper settings page, and — more importantly — guarantees you can always undo a change.

The system side of things was even less visible: the model adapter (`llm-pi-ai` providers and models), the profile's `llm-deepseek` adapter, and the active `agent-default-model` all live in the profile's settings document, editable only by hand in YAML. The **System Plugin Studio** panel reads that document live, renders a form for every parameter a plugin exposes as *volatile* (editable per profile), and edits it back through the Host — with the same staged-then-flushed discipline and one-click restore as the tool side.

- **Full tool catalog** — all 31 registered tools, grouped into 11 categories, each with a description and a complete parameter reference (type, required flag, default, enum values, minimums).
- **Stored-default editing** — expand any tool and change its configurable parameters: numbers with minimums, booleans, free strings, and enum selects.
- **Enable / disable** — toggle a tool on or off with a switch.
- **Inline validation** — every value is validated against the catalog (type, enum membership, minimum bounds) *before* it is stored. Invalid input never persists; the error is shown right next to the field.
- **Restore at every level** — reset a single parameter, restore one tool to factory state, or **Restore all defaults** (with confirmation). The store keeps only *deviations* from the catalog, so restoring is an exact inverse and can never lose anything else.
- **System Plugin Studio panel** — a second sidebar/main panel that scans the live DSH settings document and renders a schema-driven form for every system plugin whose parameters are *volatile* (editable per profile): model adapters, the active model, and friends. Dictionaries, arrays, enums, booleans, numbers, JSON, read

This package is a **DSH bundle** — install it from the Plugins page:

1. Open **Plugins** in the DSH sidebar → **Add plugin**.
2. Paste the repository URL: `https://github.com/yqd-coder/dsh-tool-config-studio.git`
3. Confirm. The plugin manager fetches the repo, installs it into your profile, and enables the bundle — a **Tool Config Studio** entry appears in the sidebar, and the bundle row (toggleable) is listed under Plugins.
Uninstalling or toggling the bundle off removes the panel; your stored configuration (localStorage) is kept.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/yqd-coder/dsh-tool-config-studio.git
cd dsh-tool-config-studio
npm run demo

```

The demo imports the real plugin source, so it must be served over `http://` (ES import attributes are not available from `file://`). `npm run demo` starts the bundled zero-dependency static server; set `PORT` to change the port.

```sh
npm test
```

The suite uses Node's built-in test runner (`node --test test/`) — no framework, no installation step. 83 tests cover catalog integrity, the store, validation, persistence, end-to-end UI smoke tests for both panels, the system schema/store/app units, and the built DSH bundle's loader contract — including that `apply` stays re-runnable across a module teardown, the way an in-place plugin update does it.

readme.text: > `dsh-tool-config-studio/client` is the **built DSH module bundle** (a browser classic script for the DSH loader, not for direct `import`). Custom hosts should use the ESM source at `/src/client.js`.

readme.section: How the DSH bundle is wired
readme.text:
| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch: inserts one row, `tool-config-studio`, named after this package |
| `package.json` | `dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client` (web platform), entry-point `exports` map |
| `lib/client.js` | Built browser module bundle — registers with `window.__ModuleLoader__`, injects the CSS, and provides `apply(ctx)` |
| `lib/index.js` | Host loader entry (browser-only plugin → no-op `apply()`) |
| `locale/{en,zh}.json` | UI string dictionaries (plus the bundle card `meta.title`) |

readme.section: How the DSH bundle is wired
readme.text: The row's browser half is loaded by DSH's client module system: the bundle materializes lazily, registers a sidebar panel and a main panel via `ctx.slots`, and mounts the same `mountToolConfigStudio` UI the demo uses. See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for the full module contract.

1. **The catalog** (`src/core/catalog.json`) is the single source of truth: every tool, parameter, type, default, enum, and minimum.
2. **The store keeps overrides only** — a value is stored only when it differs from the catalog default; the effective value is `override ?? default`.
3. **Restoring is deleting** — "reset", "restore tool", and "restore all" simply drop overrides, which is the exact inverse of editing.
The full specification — including the storage document format and the validation error codes — is in [docs/configuration-model.md](docs/configuration-model.md).

1. **The Host owns the settings document** — a layered tree where the system default sits beneath your profile override; `describe()` reports the resolved value, the base, the override, the schema, and a document revision.
2. **Only volatile fields are editable** — a schema field is visible in the panel only when the plugin marks it volatile for the active profile; that is the Host's line between "safe to tune" and "deployment-level".
3. **Editing is an op on a revision** — the panel stages edits locally, then flushes a `mutate` (set/unset ops) or a `replace` (restore) carrying the revision it read; a stale revision is rejected and the panel re-describes.

> **What the System Plugin Studio cannot touch.** `dsh-persona`, `dsh-system-prompt`, and `dsh-agent-instructions` expose *zero* volatile fields, so personas, system prompts, and agent instructions are not visible or editable in this panel — they are deployment-level settings. The panel shows a note to this effect instead of pretending otherwise.

```
├── build/           client.mjs — zero-dependency build of the DSH browser bundle
├── cordis.patch.yml Bundle patch (row: tool-config-studio)
├── demo/            Standalone demo page + zero-dependency static server
├── docs/            architecture.md, configuration-model.md

| Export (from `/src/client.js`) | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `mountToolConfigStudio(container, options?)` | Mount the tool panel UI; returns `{ store, app, unmount }` |
| `mountSystemPluginStudio(container, options?)` | Mount the System Plugin Studio UI; takes `{ adapter, i18n?, language? }`, returns `{ store, unmount }` |
| `ToolConfigStore` | The overrides-only state machine (`setParam`, `setEnabled`, `restoreTool`, `restoreAll`, `toJSON`, `fromJSON`, `subscribe`) |
| `SystemPluginStore(adapter)` | Staged-edit state machine over the settings remote (`stageSet`, `stageUnset`, `save`, `restoreAll`, `subscribe`) |
| `buildFormTree(schema, value)`, `describeLeaf(node)`, `parseLeaf(leafType, text)`, `applyOpsToValue(value, ops)` | Schemastery traversal + leaf (de)serialization helpers |
| `createLocalPersistence(storage?, key?)` | localStorage-backed persistence with safe failure modes |
| `createI18n(language?)` / `detectLanguage()` | UI translation bundle / language detection |
| `createToolConfigApp({ root, store, i18n })` | The DOM controller, usable without `mountToolConfigStudio` |
| `validateParamValue(param, value)` / `validateOverride(tool, param, value)` | The validation pre
